Regarding the effectiveness of the described physical therapy techniques for lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow): The combination of manual therapy, eccentric strengthening exercises for the wrist extensors, and ice therapy is considered highly effective and aligns with current best practices in physical therapy. Eccentric strengthening is particularly well-supported by evidence as a primary intervention for promoting tendon healing and reducing pain in lateral epicondylitis. Manual therapy can help improve joint mobility and reduce soft tissue restrictions, while ice therapy serves as an appropriate adjunct for managing acute inflammation or post-exercise soreness. This multimodal approach addresses both the mechanical dysfunction and the inflammatory component of the condition.
